question: is C31's crossing a depth effect, a lambda effect, or their interaction?  C31 ran only two corners of a 2x2 and both factors moved together.

prereg_lock.note: Frozen before any C32 measurement artefact existed.  C32 was designed with knowledge of C31's results; C32.0.2 discloses exactly what was known and which degrees of freedom that creates.  The block from '## C32.0.1 Why this experiment exists' onward is copied verbatim into reports/section_c32_depth_vs_lambda.md; tests/test_depth_vs_lambda.py asserts the copy is byte-identical and that this file's mtime strictly precedes every C32 artefact.

comparator: C31's oracle-selected best-of-N curves, read and never regenerated (gate G5)
uncertainty: per-seed values and a seed-level t interval on 2 df (t_0.975,2 = 4.302653); no bootstrap anywhere in C32

G1.rule: run_ksweep_cell, imported from C31 and redirected to a fresh C32 directory, reproduces its C31 counterpart exactly: hit-rate residual 0.0 and token residual 0.0 per generation seed, molecules identical

G2.rule: the C31 target intervals, windows and head checkpoints C32 steers with are unchanged: file hashes match C31's record and every head tensor is identical to the one C31 used

G5.rule: the oracle-selected best-of-N curve C32 prices against is byte-identical to C31's, and no C32 stage samples a best-of-N pool

G4.rule_as_preregistered: C32.0.4: d - a == depth_main + lambda_main + interaction to within 1e-12 -- THIS CLAIM IS ARITHMETICALLY FALSE, see preregistration_defects.D1
G4.rule_as_scored: the identities that actually hold for the pre-registered quantities: d - a == depth_main + lambda_main, and interaction == 0.5*((d-b)-(c-a)), both to within 1e-12

effective_lambda.definition: lambda_eff = lambda * spread(prop, M) / spread(prop, 12); the deployed envelope is interpolated linearly in log2(lambda) between bracketing measured points -- C29's rule, reused
effective_lambda.caveat: the lambda-rescale identity is pointwise in log q; the spread ratio is a scalar moment ratio of q, so this is a FIRST-ORDER CONTROL, not an identity -- C29's caveat, inherited

D1.rule: lambda dominates: |lambda_main| - |depth_main| >= 0.02 on >= 2 of 3 properties at >= 1 primary k

D2.rule: depth dominates: |depth_main| - |lambda_main| >= 0.02 on >= 2 of 3 properties at >= 1 primary k

D3.rule: the interaction is material: |interaction| >= 0.02 with a t interval excluding zero, on >= 2 of 3 properties at >= 1 primary k

D4.rule: depth survives the effective-lambda correction: depth_corrected > 0 with a t interval excluding zero, on >= 2 of 3 properties at >= 1 primary k, among non-extrapolated contrasts

D5.rule: the correction removes most of the depth effect: median confound share >= 0.5

D6.rule: the crossing is reachable without depth: at least one (12, lambda=2) cell at k <= 4 crosses the oracle curve

D7.rule: the honesty rule: any contrast whose between-seed sd exceeds its own absolute mean is reported as NOT RESOLVED at three generation seeds

P1.statement: G1 passes with residual exactly 0.0 on both gate cells, molecules included

P2.statement: the spread ratio at M exceeds 1.0 for all three properties

P3.statement: the spread ratio exceeds C29's largest (1.512) for at least one property

P4.statement: the lambda main effect is positive at k = 2 on all three properties

P5.statement: the depth main effect is positive at k = 2 on all three properties

P6.statement: D3 fires: the interaction is material on >= 2 of 3 properties

P7.statement: the median confound share is >= 0.50, i.e. D5 fires

P8.statement: D4 fires: depth survives the correction on >= 2 of 3 properties

P9.statement: D6 fires: (12, lambda=2) crosses at k <= 4 on at least one property -- STATED IN ADVANCE AS EXPECTED TO FAIL

P11.statement: validity stays >= 0.95 in every 2x2 cell (envelope cells at lambda >= 3 are not covered)

P10.statement: qed shows the smallest depth main effect of the three properties at k = 2

D1.why: with the pre-registered 0.5 convention, depth_main + lambda_main is already exactly d - a (the two marginal contrasts partition the corner difference), so adding the interaction over-counts.  The interaction is a separate contrast, not a third additive component of d - a.  Substituting a = 0, b = 1, c = 2, d = 5 gives depth = 3, lambda = 2, interaction = 1: depth + lambda = 5 = d - a, while depth + lambda + interaction = 6.
D1.handling: the defect is REPORTED and the pre-registration is NOT amended, following C29 section C29.4's handling of its own R4 defect and C27's of its gate 4.  The three effect definitions themselves are unchanged and are standard; only the closure claim was wrong, and G4 is scored on the identities that do hold.  No decision rule reads the closure identity, so no rule changes.

verdict.committed_wording: the crossing is mostly a steering-strength effect; the probe-point selection step can be dropped from the recipe
verdict.rule: C32.0.6: LAMBDA-DOMINATED iff D1 and not D2; DEPTH-DOMINATED iff D2 and not D1; INTERACTION-DOMINATED iff D3 and neither; MIXED otherwise; UNINTERPRETABLE overrides
